Exp. 1 rule sources (n=58, single trajectory; Table 2):
- No rules (baseline) + Claude Code + Opus 4.6: 50.0%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Random rule files + Claude Code + Opus 4.6: 63.8% (vs baseline p=.077). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Curated rules: 63.8% (p=.115). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Popular: 60.3% (p=.361). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Mismatched domain: 58.6% (p=.424). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Matched domain: 56.9% (p=.481). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Shuffled: 56.9% (p=.523). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- Native-only CLAUDE.md: 56.9% (p=.556). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
Exp. 2 rule counts 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50 x 3 seeds (n=58): all in the 59-67% band; 0 rules 60.3%, 50 rules 66.7% (Cochran's Q p=0.227; Fig. 3a). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
Exp. 3 rule types, 10 rules each (n=58; Table 3): tool/process 63.8%, mixed 62.1%, safety 60.3%, code style 56.9%, architecture 53.4% (Cochran's Q p=0.549). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
Exp. 4 (n=35):
- 18-rule curated set: 65.7%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors
- 4a ablation (18 leave-one-out variants): 3 shaping rules, all 'do not' (removing 'no unrelated refactor' -20pp, p=.016); 4 distorting, all 'do' (read test files, follow code style, handle edge cases, preserve compatibility); 11 inert (|delta|<=5pp)
- 4b ablation (single rules on 17 baseline-solved tasks): 14 of 18 rules break >=2 tasks (worst 4/17)
- 4c ablation (5 rule pairs; no-rule baselines 68.6-74.3%): 3 of 5 approximately additive (error <10pp), max error 22.9pp

Tasks: 58 (Exp. 1-3) / 35 (Exp. 4) discriminative SWE-bench Verified tasks, paired within-subject. Configurations: rule sources (8), counts (19 incl. seeds), types (5), ablation/distortion/superposition. Baseline: no rule file. Held constant: agent (Claude Code), model (Claude Opus 4.6 via Bedrock), prompt template, tooling; only the CLAUDE.md contents vary. Acceptance tests: SWE-bench harness. Repetitions: 1 trajectory per task-condition in Exp. 1; 3 seeds in Exp. 2; screening 3 runs. Human intervention: none

All rule conditions beat no-rule by 6.9-13.8pp but none significantly (no pairwise McNemar p<0.05; Cochran's Q p=0.697); sign test across 7 directions p=0.008. Random = curated (63.8%). No degradation with rule count up to 50. Tool/process rules best, architecture worst (10.4pp, n.s.). Polarity separation of shaping vs distorting rules Fisher p=0.029 (threshold-sensitive: dissolves at 10pp; Mann-Whitney p~0.13)

Partly: distinguished direction but rarely significance (n=58 detects ~15pp effects). Repeatable: baseline differs between Exp. 1 (50.0%) and Exp. 2 (60.3%), retest reliability 88.2% on solved tasks; run-to-run stochasticity acknowledged. Limitations stated: single agent, model, benchmark; selection bias of discriminative tasks; no multiple-comparison correction for per-rule results

Single vendor/model/benchmark (Claude Code + Opus 4.6, SWE-bench Verified, Python bug fixes); weaker models and benchmarks rewarding broader changes may differ; limited statistical power; baseline variance between experiments; per-rule significance would not survive correction; task selection bias. Future: cross-agent and cross-task replication, minimal-prime test, constraint-aware rule evolution, rules as RL reward signals
